oh also, i know u said something about a encoder/decoder so i had this made u can have this slice pack its capability into the pipeline here What you got: @reactjit/image

  Since there's no node/bun, this is a native codec fronted by a clean JS API. The key design
  choice solves your exact pain: the heavy raw RGBA never crosses into JS. You hand
  compressed bytes (or a base64 string straight from a model) in, and a small compressed
  buffer comes back — decode→resize→encode all happen in one Zig call.

  import { image } from '@reactjit/image';

  // the AI-image case: shrink + recompress in one line
  const small = image(base64FromModel).resize(1024).webp({ quality: 80 }).toBuffer();

  image(pngBytes).resize(512, 512, { fit: 'cover' }).jpeg().toFile('thumb.jpg');
  const { width, height, format } = image(bytes).metadata();   // no full decode
  const { rgba } = image(bytes).raw();                          // pixels for a shader/canvas

  Formats: PNG + JPEG (already-vendored stb), resize (newly-vendored stb_image_resize2), and
  WebP via libwebp — dlopen'd lazily (sqlite3-style), so PNG/JPEG-only carts never load it
  and it "just works" where libwebp is present.

  Verified end-to-end (./tools/rjit shot image_demo, ALL PASS):

  ┌─────────────────────────┬─────────┐
  │          stage          │  size   │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────┤
  │ 512² RGBA raw           │ 1024 KB │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────┤
  │ → PNG                   │ 59.9 KB │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────┤
  │ → resize 128 → JPEG q80 │ 1.7 KB  │
  ├─────────────────────────┼─────────┤
  │ → resize 128 → WebP q80 │ 0.6 KB  │
  └─────────────────────────┴─────────┘

  toFile wrote a real 128×128 JPEG to disk (file confirms it).

  How it's wired

  It's a gated ingredient — importing @reactjit/image auto-triggers -Dhas-imageops via the
  metafile gate (same mechanism as frame-capture), so carts that don't use it pay zero
  bytes/host-fns. New files: framework/image/codec.zig, framework/v8_bindings_image_ops.zig,
  runtime/image.ts, cart/image_demo.tsx, vendored stb_image_resize2. Touched: build.zig,
  v8_ingredients.zig, dependency-registry.json (+ a libwebp entry), ship.ts.
resolution: Captured the new @reactjit/image native codec (decode→resize→encode PNG/JPEG/WebP in one Zig call; runtime/image.ts + framework/image/codec.zig, gated imageops ingredient) as a capability to fold into the next slice. Verified it exists + its API (image(b64).resize().webp().toBuffer()). This is the decoder I'd flagged as missing — it enables real compression in/out, external-image-seeded img2img, and tiny WebP cooked-asset thumbnails. Folded into the asset-compiler handoff with the guidance to adopt it in the cook step (where the imageops rebuild lands for free) and NOT retrofit it into the now-hot-reloadable AI fill. No code change this session — it's a build-ready capability the next slice consumes.
